groups.text: It is currently 14 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Researchers are struggling to predict how AI models will actually behave once they reach the public. Marcus Williams and his colleagues found that most pre-deployment safety evaluations lack sufficient coverage and are too easily recognized as tests to be representative. To fix this, they developed a method to simulate deployment by using de-identified conversations from previous releases to estimate misbehavior rates. They tested this approach across four GPT-5-series deployments, finding it more informative than baselines using adversarially selected data. In a separate effort to apply machine learning to healthcare, Roy Segal and his team introduced STST-JEPA. This self-supervised transformer aims to improve the accuracy of brain-age biomarkers inferred from EEG recordings. The researchers pretrained the model on over 47,000 sessions to overcome common hurdles like small labeled cohorts and variations in how different sites record brain activity.

The United States has renewed military strikes against Iran's military infrastructure, hitting roughly 90 targets overnight on July 8th and 9th. President Donald Trump announced that a fragile ceasefire between the two parties is now over. These attacks targeted logistics, missile and drone storage sites, and air defense systems. The retaliation follows Iranian strikes on civilian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on July 7th, leading the president to call Iranian leadership "scum." In response, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims it launched strikes on U.S. military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. Meanwhile, a separate legal matter has concluded in Manhattan. A U.S. District Judge ordered that $5.8 million be paid to writer E. Jean Carroll. The funds, held in escrow since 2023 after a jury found the president guilty of sexual abuse and defamation, are now being released because the judge ruled Trump had been stalling the case.

Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries have triggered a widespread fuel crisis across several Russian regions. Kyiv has now targeted Russia's ten largest refineries, including a July 6th attack on the Omsk facility located 2,500 kilometers from the Ukrainian border. This has left motorists driving through cities in search of open stations, with some sleeping in their cars for days and engaging in scuffles while waiting for fuel. Some residents report that traders are exacerbating the shortage by buying up gasoline to resell it at inflated prices. In other news, France and Morocco will face each other this Thursday in the World Cup quarter-finals. The two teams last met in a semi-final four years ago in Qatar, which France won two-nil. While the French side is aiming for its third consecutive world semi-final, Morocco enters the match with one of the most talented squads in its history.

Memory costs remain a primary hurdle for long-context autoregressive inference because the key-value cache dominates system resources. To address this, researcher Vladimir Gusev proposes Fractal KV-Cache Archives, using contractive iterated-map codes to serialize symbol sequences into low-dimensional real vectors. This lossless method supports random access and amortized append in linear time. In tests using GPT-2 with 1024-token contexts, per-head residual vector quantization reduced the archived cache by 36 to 54 times compared to an fp16 cache, though it increased perplexity by 11 to 15 percent. Shifting from memory storage to data classification, a separate team has introduced TimEE. This 4.5 million parameter foundation model enables end-to-end time series classification via in-context learning. By using a single forward pass without per-dataset training, TimEE ranks first in ROC AUC on the UCR benchmark, despite being meta-trained exclusively on synthetic tasks rather than real time series.

Renaissance Africa Energy is moving to develop the JK field in the Niger Delta. The company recently announced a significant oil discovery that could accelerate the commercialization of the site. This onshore asset was first drilled back in 1967 by Shell, but it has remained dormant for nearly six decades. By targeting this specific field, Renaissance Africa Energy aims to bring new production to an area where resources have sat untouched since the late sixties. The move signals a shift toward reviving older, neglected assets to boost energy output in Nigeria.

Reinforcement learning is becoming increasingly important for the post-training of large language models. For long-horizon agentic tasks, previous pipelines were mostly synchronous and batch-interleaved, which proved inefficient. Asynchronous reinforcement learning has emerged as a more efficient alternative because it updates the model as rollouts arrive. However, existing asynchronous systems often prioritize throughput over training stability and task effectiveness. To address these stability and off-policy challenges, researchers Zhenyu Hou and his colleagues have introduced Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization, or SAO. This method replaces group-wise sampling with single-rollout sampling to improve generalization. The team also implemented a strict double-side token-level clipping strategy to ensure optimization stability. These combined designs allow the system to train stably for one thousand steps.

Uzbekistan’s deputies have passed a law to modify the nation's Latin-based alphabet. The new system may consist of twenty-eight letters and an apostrophe, replacing the previous structure of twenty-six letters and three digraphs. This legislation moved through the Legislative Chamber in three readings without a single vote against it. It now awaits approval from the Senate. Notably, the draft law was not published for public discussion; only a version from 2021 remains available on the government's legislative portal. For historical context, Uzbekistan first introduced the Latin alphabet in 1993 to move away from the Cyrillic system used during the Soviet period. This follows a long history of shifts, including a 1929 transition from Arabic calligraphy and a later shift back to Cyrillic in 1940. The current changes mark another step in the country's evolving approach to its written language.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be mostly clear with temperatures between 20 and 25 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Sommerferien 2026 Berlin, at 14:00, Meeting Aaron, at 17:40, Agentur für Arbeit, and at 19:00, ️ Greifen and ️ Greifen.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
